content.title: New Single Family Permit
content.summary: Building a new home in Arvada requires a building permit, and if the lot exceeds 10,000 square feet, a site development permit is also necessary. Applicants must submit various documents, including architectural, structural, and foundation plans, along with specific details for custom and mastered homes, ensuring compliance with the city's design criteria and adopted codes. Additional requirements may apply for sprinklered homes, including fire department approvals and specific engineering documentation.
content.body:
## Before You Apply

Thinking about building a new home in Arvada? A building permit is required for constructing new buildings, structures and their accessories. If the lot is over 10,000 square feet, a site development permit must also be obtained. If the home is sprinklered, additional fire department requirements for permits and plans may be required to be provided.

## Required Documents

The following are the required documents that must be filled out completely and submitted along with the online permit application through [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]). The permit will not be accepted if there are missing plans, documents or information. All plans should be submitted as individual PDF documents, and there should be no security-locked documents submitted. Please verify that all design criteria, design conditions and adopted codes match what has been adopted by the City of Arvada before submitting. Design conditions, code information and design criteria are listed below.

## For Custom Homes

Custom Home build plans will need to be site specific with the address or lot/block listed on all plans. Plans and applications must include the proposed square footages. Multi-unit buildings must include details showing construction of rated walls/assemblies between units. Plans and any engineer letters must also include the applicable [design criteria and adopted codes for the City of Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/165/Adopted-Building-Code). If the home/ homes are sprinklered, please reference the type of sprinkler system on the architectural plans and additional plans and submittal requirements may be required by the applicable fire district.

It will require:

- Plot Plan. The plot plan should include fire separation distances and requirements.
- Erosion/Grading Plan
- Architectural Plans: Building Elevations, Cross Sections, Floor Plans, details, thermal envelope details, etc. (See Note 1)
- Structural Plans, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Foundation Plans, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Soils Report, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Set of Manual J, D and S Calculations
- Energy Report- calculation of Building Envelope Compliance (See Note 3)
- Truss Specification Package, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Gas line sizing calculation and schematic drawing
- Radon Control Method Detail

**Notes:**

- **Note 1**: See the most current version of the Colorado Revised Statutes 12-25-303 for requirements on when architectural stamped plans are required.
- **Note 2**: By a design professional licensed in the State of Colorado (ie. engineer or architect).
- **Note 3**: Only required when using a performance or energy rated index (ERI) based method of compliance to demonstrate building envelope compliance requirements and other energy code requirements (some examples of an energy report include REScheck- for performance or HER's report- for ERI method).

## For Mastered Homes

Master plans are allowed to reference addresses for cross streets and subdivision names as long as the referenced addresses, cross streets and subdivision information are accurate for the full scope of the project included in the plan set being mastered. Plans and applications must include the proposed square footages. Multi-unit buildings must include details showing construction of rated walls/assemblies between units. Plans and any engineer letters must also include the applicable [design criteria and adopted codes for the City of Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/165/Adopted-Building-Code). If the home/ homes are sprinklered, please reference the type of sprinkler system on the architectural plans and additional plans and submittal requirements may be required by the applicable fire district.

- Architectural Plans: Building Elevations, Cross Sections, Floor Plans, details, thermal envelope details, etc. (See Note 1)
- Structural Plans, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Foundation Plans, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Truss Specification Package, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
- Gas line sizing calculation and schematic drawing
- Radon Control Method Detail (can be included):
	- Soils Report, Stamped and Signed (See Note 2)
		- Set of Manual JDS Calculations (for townhomes, one manual JDS can be provided for each of the end unit type models and each of the internal unit type models, with exposure show to the worst case scenario- west for the front door)
		- Energy Report- calculation of Building Envelope Compliance (See Note 3)

**Notes:**

- **Note 1**: See the most current version of the Colorado Revised Statutes 12-25-303 for requirements on when architectural stamped plans are required.
- **Note 2**: By a design professional licensed in the State of Colorado (engineer or architect).
- **Note 3**: Only required when using a performance or energy rated index (ERI) based method of compliance to demonstrate building envelope compliance requirements and other energy code requirements (some examples of an energy report include REScheck- for performance or HER's report- for ERI method).

## For Repeat Plan Sets From Master

Repeat home plans will need to be site specific with the address or lot/block listed on all plans. Any engineer letters must include the applicable [design criteria and adopted codes for the City of Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/165/Adopted-Building-Code).

- Plot Plan. The plot plan should include fire separation distances and requirements.
- Erosion/Grading Plan

## Submitting an Application

Applications are submitted using our customer portal. Please log in with your AEC number that was assigned to your company. Applications are only available to licensed contractors. If you are a homeowner that will be constructing a new single family home, please contact the building division directly to apply for a permit and please be aware that we may require a homeowners license as well.


## Required Approvals

Approvals for permit issuance are required from Planning, Engineering, stormwater and the Building Division. Occasionally the fire department may have to review and approve as well. After the application is accepted, a review will be sent to the review team. Each review cycle will be 15 business days for repeat permits. For master and custom permits the review will be 20 business days and 10 business days for subsequent reviews. After the review cycle, all plans and documents will be flattened and uploaded to the permit file. A notice of approval or disapproval will be emailed to the applicant of the permit through our permitting system, with direction for next steps. If revisions are requested, you must submit the updated plans and documents that were required from each department, through the customer permitting portal for additional review. During our review cycle you will not be able to view staff comments.

**Note**: If your application is associated with a development project, the application will not be approved until the Development Application has received approval.

## Inspections

Inspections can be scheduled until 6 a.m. of the desired inspection date. Inspections are completed Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. All inspections can be scheduled using the Permit Portal or by calling 720-898-7630 and using the automated line. A 3-digit inspection code is required. NEW! We have a texting inspection option as well. [View the new inspection scheduling instructions on this page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1243/Inspection-Scheduling-Instructions-and-A).

## Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.)

To obtain a Certificate of Occupancy the project must be in good standing with Engineering, Planning, Building, Utilities, Fire and Stormwater. All fees must be paid prior to an issuance of the C.O.

## Step 1: All Final Inspections Are Completed
- Final Structural
- Final Electrical
- Final Mechanical (HVAC) 
- Final Plumbing
- CO-Public Improvement

## Step 2: Upload Required Documents

All documents should be uploaded to the permit through the [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]). **All documents must be uploaded individually in PDF format. A CO/TCO checklist will be provided for your specific project and will be attached to each applicable permit, for your convenience. If you do not have a checklist, please reach out to us and we can provide you with a copy.**

Provide the following:

- Air Leakage Report/Blower Door Certification - less than or equal to 3 ACH per minute
- Energy certification, if using the performance-based method
- HERs report if using the ERI: Energy rated index method
- Insulation certificate for all compliance methods
- Documentation of compliance with section R302.13 of the 2018 IRC for fire protection of floor assemblies (the documentation that needs to be submitted depends on what method was used for compliance). Please ask us if you have any questions.
- The Foundation Inspection Form, with each of the required inspections signed and stamped by the engineer that approved the inspection. See Foundation Inspection Form for details.
- Final ILC w/ impervious surface calculation
- Final Grading Certificate
- [Certificate of Landscaping Completion (PDF)](https://www.arvadaco.gov/DocumentCenter/View/278)
	- If landscape construction is partially completed, or is yet to start construction, the Landscape Architect must provide an estimate indicating the value of the incomplete landscaping; this will serve as the basis for the required escrow amount as established by the development agreement. If there is no effective development agreement for the site, the required escrow amount will be set at 150% of the estimated value, except during a drought, during which time the escrow may be reduced to 110% of the contract value for incomplete turf or seeded areas, trees, shrubs, mulch, edger, and weed barrier; a factor of 150% will be applied to all other landscape elements. Escrowed funds will be released upon submission of Certificate of Landscape Completion indicating that 100% of the landscape design for the site has been completed per the approved plans.
- Statement of Special Inspections and Special Inspection letters
	- Occasionally, special inspections are required for single family homes, townhomes and duplexes. Please check with your design professionals to see if a statement of special inspections should be added to your plans and ask if you have any questions on this.

## Step 3: Schedule a CO/TCO Inspection

This will notify the other departments a CO or TCO is being requested. Please be aware that this is not an actual inspection but rather a step in the process. Missing documentation or inspections may result in a denial of this request. If your request is denied, please ensure you have completed all required inspections and attached all required documents and schedule this again to restart the process. Once your request is accepted, please be aware that the review process will take 3-5 business days to be completed. Please plan your project accordingly.

## Step 4: Pay Fees

1. **Pay your tap fees**. If paying fees with non-certified funds, you must allow for the payment to clear before you will be approved for a Certificate of Occupancy.
2. **Landscaping Escrow**: If the landscape is incomplete, the planner will assess the escrow amount on the permit. This must be paid before CO/TCO can be issued.

## Step 5: Monitor the Permit Portal

Once the CO/TCO inspection step has been accepted, reviews will be sent out to all required departments. Monitor [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]) to make sure all of the reviews are completed by the following departments:

- Engineering
- Planning
- Utility Billing
- Building

After all departments have approved their reviews, a Certificate of Occupancy may be issued. An email will be sent to the permit applicant when the permit status is updated. Please allow 3 to 5 business days for this full CO/TCO review process to be completed and plan your project timeline accordingly.

## Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (T.C.O)
A Temporary Certificate of Occupancy can be requested, please complete the steps for a Certificate of Occupancy and [email Building Permits Division](mailto:buildingpermits@arvada.org) with details for your request for a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy
